Custom threshold (in range 0-1) for adjusting mesh internals detection based on the percentage of test rays hit triangle backfaces. Use lower value for more dense mesh.
Enables using GPU for SDF generation, otherwise CPU will be used (async via Job System).

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Matrix.Orthogonalize
member.summary: Orthogonalizes the specified matrix.

remarks.para: Orthogonalization is the process of making all rows orthogonal to each other. This means that any given row in the matrix will be orthogonal to any other given row in the matrix.

Because this method uses the modified Gram-Schmidt process, the resulting matrix tends to be numerically unstable. The numeric stability decreases according to the rows so that the first row is the most stable and the last row is the least stable.
This operation is performed on the rows of the matrix rather than the columns. If you wish for this operation to be performed on the columns, first transpose the input and than transpose the output.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Matrix.Orthonormalize
member.summary: Orthonormalizes the specified matrix.

remarks.para: Orthonormalization is the process of making all rows and columns orthogonal to each other and making all rows and columns of unit length. This means that any given row will be orthogonal to any other given row and any given column will be orthogonal to any other given column. Any given row will not be orthogonal to any given column. Every row and every column will be of unit length.

Because this method uses the modified Gram-Schmidt process, the resulting matrix tends to be numerically unstable. The numeric stability decreases according to the rows so that the first row is the most stable and the last row is the least stable.
This operation is performed on the rows of the matrix rather than the columns. If you wish for this operation to be performed on the columns, first transpose the input and than transpose the output.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Matrix.Orthogonalize(FlaxEngine.Matrix@,FlaxEngine.Matrix@)
member.summary: Orthogonalizes the specified matrix.
member.param: When the method completes, contains the orthogonalized matrix.

remarks.para: Orthogonalization is the process of making all rows orthogonal to each other. This means that any given row in the matrix will be orthogonal to any other given row in the matrix.

Because this method uses the modified Gram-Schmidt process, the resulting matrix tends to be numerically unstable. The numeric stability decreases according to the rows so that the first row is the most stable and the last row is the least stable.
This operation is performed on the rows of the matrix rather than the columns. If you wish for this operation to be performed on the columns, first transpose the input and than transpose the output.

remarks.para: Orthonormalization is the process of making all rows and columns orthogonal to each other and making all rows and columns of unit length. member.summary: Brings the matrix into upper triangular form using elementary row operations.
member.param: The matrix to put into upper triangular form.

member.remarks: If the matrix is not invertible (i.e. its determinant is zero) than the result of this method may produce Single.Nan and Single.Inf values. member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Matrix.ReducedRowEchelonForm(FlaxEngine.Matrix@,FlaxEngine.Float4@,FlaxEngine.Matrix@,FlaxEngine.Float4@)
member.summary: Brings the matrix into reduced row echelon form using elementary row operations.
member.param: The matrix to put into reduced row echelon form.
The fifth column of the matrix.
When the method completes, contains the resultant matrix after the operation.
When the method completes, contains the resultant fifth column of the matrix.

remarks.para: The fifth column is often called the augmented part of the matrix. This is because the fifth column is really just an extension of the matrix so that there is a place to put all of the non-zero components after the operation is complete.
Often times the resultant matrix will the identity matrix or a matrix similar to the identity matrix. Sometimes, however, that is not possible and numbers other than zero and one may appear.

This method can be used to solve systems of linear equations. Upon completion of this method, the will contain the solution for the system. It is up to the user to analyze both the input and the result to determine if a solution really exists.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Matrix3x3.Orthogonalize
member.summary: Orthogonalizes the specified Matrix3x3.

remarks.para: Orthogonalization is the process of making all rows orthogonal to each other. This means that any given row in the Matrix3x3 will be orthogonal to any other given row in the Matrix3x3.

Because this method uses the modified Gram-Schmidt process, the resulting Matrix3x3 tends to be numerically unstable. The numeric stability decreases according to the rows so that the first row is the most stable and the last row is the least stable.

This operation is performed on the rows of the Matrix3x3 rather than the columns. If you wish for this operation to be performed on the columns, first transpose the input and than transpose the output.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Matrix3x3.Orthonormalize
member.summary: Orthonormalizes the specified Matrix3x3.

remarks.para: Orthonormalization is the process of making all rows and columns orthogonal to each other and making all rows and columns of unit length. This means that any given row will be orthogonal to any other given row and any given column will be orthogonal to any other given column. Any given row will not be orthogonal to any given column. Every row and every column will be of unit length.

Because this method uses the modified Gram-Schmidt process, the resulting Matrix3x3 tends to be numerically unstable. The numeric stability decreases according to the rows so that the first row is the most stable and the last row is the least stable.

This operation is performed on the rows of the Matrix3x3 rather than the columns. If you wish for this operation to be performed on the columns, first transpose the input and than transpose the output.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Matrix3x3.Orthogonalize(FlaxEngine.Matrix3x3@,FlaxEngine.Matrix3x3@)
member.summary: Orthogonalizes the specified Matrix3x3.
member.param: When the method completes, contains the orthogonalized Matrix3x3.

remarks.para: Orthogonalization is the process of making all rows orthogonal to each other. This means that any given row in the Matrix3x3 will be orthogonal to any other given row in the Matrix3x3.

Because this method uses the modified Gram-Schmidt process, the resulting Matrix3x3 tends to be numerically unstable. The numeric stability decreases according to the rows so that the first row is the most stable and the last row is the least stable.

This operation is performed on the rows of the Matrix3x3 rather than the columns. If you wish for this operation to be performed on the columns, first transpose the input and than transpose the output.

member.summary: Orthonormalizes the specified Matrix3x3.
member.param: When the method completes, contains the orthonormalized Matrix3x3.

remarks.para: Orthonormalization is the process of making all rows and columns orthogonal to each other and making all rows and columns of unit length. This means that any given row will be orthogonal to any other given row and any given column will be orthogonal to any other given column. Any given row will not be orthogonal to any given column. Every row and every column will be of unit length.

Because this method uses the modified Gram-Schmidt process, the resulting Matrix3x3 tends to be numerically unstable. The numeric stability decreases according to the rows so that the first row is the most stable and the last row is the least stable.

This operation is performed on the rows of the Matrix3x3 rather than the columns. If you wish for this operation to be performed on the columns, first transpose the input and than transpose the output.

member.summary: Performs a coordinate transformation using the given .
member.param: When the method completes, contains the transformed coordinates.
member.remarks: A coordinate transform performs the transformation with the assumption that the w component is one. The four dimensional vector obtained from the transformation operation has each component in the vector divided by the w component. This forces the w component to be one and therefore makes the vector homogeneous. The homogeneous vector is often preferred when working with coordinates as the w component can safely be ignored.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Float2.TransformNormal(FlaxEngine.Float2@,FlaxEngine.Matrix@,FlaxEngine.Float2@)
member.summary: Performs a normal transformation using the given .
member.param: When the method completes, contains the transformed normal.
member.remarks: A normal transform performs the transformation with the assumption that the w component is zero. This causes the fourth row and fourth column of the matrix to be unused. The end result is a vector that is not translated, but all other transformation properties apply. This is often preferred for normal vectors as normals purely represent direction rather than location because normal vectors should not be translated.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Float3.TransformCoordinate(FlaxEngine.Float3@,FlaxEngine.Matrix@,FlaxEngine.Float3@)
member.summary: Performs a coordinate transformation using the given .
member.param: When the method completes, contains the transformed coordinates.
member.remarks: A coordinate transform performs the transformation with the assumption that the w component is one. The four dimensional vector obtained from the transformation operation has each component in the vector divided by the w component. This forces the w component to be one and therefore makes the vector homogeneous. The homogeneous vector is often preferred when working with coordinates as the w component can safely be ignored.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Float3.TransformNormal(FlaxEngine.Float3@,FlaxEngine.Matrix@,FlaxEngine.Float3@)
member.summary: Performs a normal transformation using the given .
member.param: When the method completes, contains the transformed normal.
member.remarks: A normal transform performs the transformation with the assumption that the w component is zero. This causes the fourth row and fourth column of the matrix to be unused. The end result is a vector that is not translated, but all other transformation properties apply. This is often preferred for normal vectors as normals purely represent direction rather than location because normal vectors should not be translated.

member.summary: Performs a coordinate transformation using the given .
member.param: When the method completes, contains the transformed coordinates.
member.remarks: A coordinate transform performs the transformation with the assumption that the w component is one. The four dimensional vector obtained from the transformation operation has each component in the vector divided by the w component. This forces the w component to be one and therefore makes the vector homogeneous. The homogeneous vector is often preferred when working with coordinates as the w component can safely be ignored.

This is often preferred for normal vectors as normals purely represent direction rather than location because normal vectors should not be translated.

member.remarks: Distance squared is the value before taking the square root. Distance squared can often be used in place of distance if relative comparisons are being made. For example, consider three points A, B, and C. To determine whether B or C is further from A, compare the distance between A and B to the distance between A and C. Calculating the two distances involves two square roots, which are computationally expensive. However, using distance squared provides the same information and avoids calculating two square roots.

member.summary: Performs a coordinate transformation using the given .
member.param: When the method completes, contains the transformed coordinates.
member.remarks: A coordinate transform performs the transformation with the assumption that the w component is one. The four dimensional vector obtained from the transformation operation has each component in the vector divided by the w component. This forces the w component to be one and therefore makes the vector homogeneous. The homogeneous vector is often preferred when working with coordinates as the w component can safely be ignored.

member.param: When the method completes, contains the transformed normal.
member.remarks: A normal transform performs the transformation with the assumption that the w component is zero. This causes the fourth row and fourth column of the matrix to be unused. The end result is a vector that is not translated, but all other transformation properties apply. This is often preferred for normal vectors as normals purely represent direction rather than location because normal vectors should not be translated.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Int3.DistanceSquared(FlaxEngine.Int3@,FlaxEngine.Int3@,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Calculates the squared distance between two vectors.
member.param: When the method completes, contains the squared distance between the two vectors.
member.remarks: Distance squared is the value before taking the square root. Distance squared can often be used in place of distance if relative comparisons are being made. For example, consider three points A, B, and C. To determine whether B or C is further from A, compare the distance between A and B to the distance between A and C. Calculating the two distances involves two square roots, which are computationally expensive. However, using distance squared provides the same information and avoids calculating two square roots.

member.name: T:FlaxEngine.GPUResourceUsage
member.summary: Identifies expected GPU resource use during rendering. The usage directly reflects whether a resource is accessible by the CPU and/or the GPU.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.GPUResourceUsage.Default
member.summary: A resource that requires read and write access by the GPU. This is likely to be the most common usage choice. Memory will be used on device only, so fast access from the device is preferred. It usually means device-local GPU (video) memory.
member.remarks: Usage: - Resources written and read by device, e.g. images used as render targets. - Resources transferred from host once (immutable) or infrequently and read by device multiple times, e.g. textures to be sampled, vertex buffers, constant buffers, and majority of other types of resources used on GPU.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.GPUResourceUsage.Dynamic
member.summary: A resource that is accessible by both the GPU (read only) and the CPU (write only). A dynamic resource is a good choice for a resource that will be updated by the CPU at least once per frame. Dynamic buffers or textures are usually used to upload data to GPU and use it within a single frame.
member.remarks: Usage: - Resources written frequently by CPU (dynamic), read by device. E.g. textures, vertex buffers, uniform buffers updated every frame or every draw call.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.GPUResourceUsage.StagingUpload
member.summary: A resource that supports data transfer (copy) from the CPU to the GPU. It usually means CPU (system) memory. Resources created in this pool may still be accessible to the device, but access to them can be slow.
member.remarks: Usage: - Staging copy of resources used as transfer source.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.GPUResourceUsage.StagingReadback
member.summary: A resource that supports data transfer (copy) from the GPU to the CPU.
member.remarks: Usage: - Resources written by device, read by host - results of some computations, e.g. screen capture, average scene luminance for HDR tone mapping. - Any resources read or accessed randomly on host, e.g. CPU-side copy of vertex buffer used as source of transfer, but also used for collision detection.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.GPUResourceUsage.Staging
member.summary: A resource that supports both read and write from the CPU. This is likely to be the common choice for read-write buffers to transfer data between GPU compute buffers and CPU memory. It usually means CPU (system) memory.
member.remarks: Usage: - Staging memory to upload to GPU for compute and gather results back after processing.

member.summary: The blend factor is (1 - Ad 1 - Ad 1 - Ad 1 - Ad), that is alpha data from a render target. The pre-blend operation inverts the data, generating 1 - A.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ToneMappingSettings.WhiteTemperature
member.summary: Adjusts the white balance in relation to the temperature of the light in the scene. When the light temperature and this one match the light will appear white. When a value is used that is higher than the light in the scene it will yield a "warm" or yellow color, and, conversely, if the value is lower, it would yield a "cool" or blue color.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ToneMappingSettings.WhiteTint
member.summary: Adjusts the white balance temperature tint for the scene by adjusting the cyan and magenta color ranges. Ideally, this setting should be used once you've adjusted the white balance temperature to get accurate colors. Under some light temperatures, the colors may appear to be more yellow or blue. This can be used to balance the resulting color to look more natural.

member.summary: The effect intensity (normalized to range [0;1]). Use 0 to disable it.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.TraceMode
member.summary: The reflections tracing mode.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.DepthResolution
member.summary: The depth buffer downscale option to optimize raycast performance. Full gives better quality, but half improves performance.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.RayTracePassResolution
member.summary: The raycast resolution. Full gives better quality, but half improves performance.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.BRDFBias
member.summary: The reflection spread parameter. This value controls source roughness effect on reflections blur. Smaller values produce wider reflections spread but also introduce more noise. Higher values provide more mirror-like reflections.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.RoughnessThreshold
member.summary: The maximum amount of roughness a material must have to reflect the scene. For example, if this value is set to 0.4, only materials with a roughness value of 0.4 or below reflect the scene.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.WorldAntiSelfOcclusionBias
member.summary: The offset of the raycast origin. Lower values produce more correct reflection placement, but produce more artifacts. We recommend values of 0.3 or lower.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.ResolvePassResolution
member.summary: The raycast resolution. Full gives better quality, but half improves performance.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.ResolveSamples
member.summary: The number of rays used to resolve the reflection color. Higher values provide better quality but reduce effect performance. Use value of 1 for the best performance at cost of quality.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.EdgeFadeFactor
member.summary: The point at which the far edges of the reflection begin to fade. Has no effect on performance.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.FadeOutDistance
member.summary: The effect fade out end distance from camera (in world units).

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.FadeDistance
member.summary: The effect fade distance (in world units). Defines the size of the effect fade from fully visible to fully invisible at FadeOutDistance.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.UseColorBufferMips
member.summary: "The input color buffer downscale mode that uses blurred mipmaps when resolving the reflection color. Produces more realistic results by blurring distant parts of reflections in rough (low-gloss) materials. It also improves performance on most platforms but uses more memory.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.TemporalEffect
member.summary: If checked, enables the temporal pass. Reduces noise, but produces an animated "jittering" effect that's sometimes noticeable. If disabled, the properties below have no effect.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.TemporalScale
member.summary: The intensity of the temporal effect. Lower values produce reflections faster, but more noise.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ScreenSpaceReflectionsSettings.TemporalResponse
member.summary: Defines how quickly reflections blend between the reflection in the current frame and the history buffer. Lower values produce reflections faster, but with more jittering. If the camera in your game doesn't move much, we recommend values closer to 1.

member.summary: Used to create fogging effects such as clouds but with a density that is related to the height of the fog.

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the .

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.FogDensity
member.summary: The fog density factor.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.FogHeightFalloff
member.summary: The fog height density factor that controls how the density increases as height decreases. Smaller values produce a more visible transition layer.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.FogInscatteringColor
member.summary: Color of the fog.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.FogMaxOpacity
member.summary: Maximum opacity of the fog. A value of 1 means the fog can become fully opaque at a distance and replace scene color completely. A value of 0 means the fog color will not be factored in at all.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.StartDistance
member.summary: Distance from the camera that the fog will start, in world units.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.FogCutoffDistance
member.summary: Scene elements past this distance will not have fog applied. This is useful for excluding skyboxes which already have fog baked in. Setting this value to 0 disables it. Negative value sets the cutoff distance relative to the far plane of the camera.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.DirectionalInscatteringLight
member.summary: Directional light used for Directional Inscattering.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.DirectionalInscatteringExponent
member.summary: Controls the size of the directional inscattering cone, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: there must be a directional light enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. Range: 2-64.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.DirectionalInscatteringStartDistance
member.summary: Controls the start distance from the viewer of the directional inscattering, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: there must be a directional light enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.DirectionalInscatteringColor
member.summary: Controls the color of the directional inscattering, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: there must be a directional light enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.VolumetricFogEnable
member.summary: Whether to enable Volumetric fog. Graphics quality settings control the resolution of the fog simulation.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.VolumetricFogScatteringDistribution
member.summary: Controls the scattering phase function - how much incoming light scatters in various directions. A distribution value of 0 scatters equally in all directions, while 0.9 scatters predominantly in the light direction. In order to have visible volumetric fog light shafts from the side, the distribution will need to be closer to 0. Range: -0.9-0.9.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.VolumetricFogAlbedo
member.summary: The height fog particle reflectiveness used by volumetric fog. Water particles in air have an albedo near white, while dust has slightly darker value.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.VolumetricFogEmissive
member.summary: Light emitted by height fog. This is a density value so more light is emitted the further you are looking through the fog. In most cases using a Skylight is a better choice, however, it may be useful in certain scenarios.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.VolumetricFogExtinctionScale
member.summary: Scales the height fog particle extinction amount used by volumetric fog. Values larger than 1 cause fog particles everywhere absorb more light. Range: 0.1-10.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.ExponentialHeightFog.VolumetricFogDistance
member.summary: Distance over which volumetric fog should be computed. Larger values extend the effect into the distance but expose under-sampling artifacts in details.

member.summary: The length of the rays for contact shadows computed via the screen-space tracing. Set this to values higher than 0 to enable screen-space shadows rendering for this light. This improves the shadowing details. Actual ray distance is based on the pixel distance from the camera.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.LightWithShadow.ShadowsUpdateRate
member.summary: Frequency of shadow updates. 1 - every frame, 0.5 - every second frame, 0 - on start or change. It's the inverse value of how many frames should happen in-between shadow map updates (eg. inverse of 0.5 is 2 thus shadow will update every 2nd frame).

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.LightWithShadow.ShadowsUpdateRateAtDistance
member.summary: Frequency of shadow updates at the maximum distance from the view at which shadows are still rendered. This value is multiplied by ShadowsUpdateRate and allows scaling the update rate in-between the shadow range. For example, if light is near view, it will get normal shadow updates but will reduce this rate when far from view. See ShadowsUpdateRate to learn more.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.LightWithShadow.ShadowsResolution
member.summary: Defines the resolution of the shadow map texture used to draw objects projection from light-point-of-view. Higher values increase shadow quality at cost of performance.

member.summary: Client gets replicated object from server but still can locally autonomously simulate it too. For example, client can control local pawn with real human input but will validate with server proper state (eg. to prevent cheats).

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.Cloth.SimulationSettings.UpdateWhenOffscreen

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.IsKinematic
member.summary: Enables kinematic mode for the rigidbody. Kinematic rigidbodies are special dynamic actors that are not influenced by forces(such as gravity), and have no momentum. They are considered to have infinite mass and can push regular dynamic actors out of the way. Kinematics will not collide with static or other kinematic objects but are great for moving platforms or characters, where direct motion control is desired.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.LinearDamping
member.summary: Gets or sets the 'drag' force added to reduce linear movement. Linear damping can be used to slow down an object. The higher the drag the more the object slows down.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.AngularDamping
member.summary: Gets or sets the 'drag' force added to reduce angular movement. Angular damping can be used to slow down the rotation of an object. The higher the drag the more the rotation slows down.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.EnableSimulation
member.summary: If true simulation and collisions detection will be enabled for the rigidbody.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.UseCCD
member.summary: If true Continuous Collision Detection (CCD) will be used for this component.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.EnableGravity
member.summary: If object should have the force of gravity applied.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.StartAwake
member.summary: If object should start awake, or if it should initially be sleeping.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.UpdateMassWhenScaleChanges
member.summary: If true, it will update mass when actor scale changes.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.MaxAngularVelocity
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum angular velocity that a simulated object can achieve. The angular velocity of rigidbodies is clamped to MaxAngularVelocity to avoid numerical instability with fast rotating bodies. Because this may prevent intentional fast rotations on objects such as wheels, you can override this value per rigidbody.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.OverrideMass
member.summary: Override the auto computed mass.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.Mass
member.summary: Gets or sets the mass value measured in kilograms (use override value only if OverrideMass is checked).

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.MassScale
member.summary: Gets or sets the per-instance scaling of the mass.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.CenterOfMassOffset
member.summary: Gets or sets the user specified offset for the center of mass of this object, from the calculated location.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.Constraints
member.summary: Gets or sets the object movement constraint flags that define degrees of freedom are allowed for the simulation of object.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.LinearVelocity
member.summary: Gets or sets the linear velocity of the rigidbody.
member.remarks: It's used mostly to get the current velocity. Manual modifications may result in unrealistic behaviour.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.AngularVelocity
member.summary: Gets or sets the angular velocity of the rigidbody measured in radians per second.
member.remarks: It's used mostly to get the current angular velocity. Manual modifications may result in unrealistic behaviour.

member.name: P:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.MaxDepenetrationVelocity
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum depenetration velocity when rigidbody moving out of penetrating state.
member.remarks: This value controls how much velocity the solver can introduce to correct for penetrations in contacts. Using this property can smooth objects moving out of colliding state and prevent unstable motion.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.AddForce(FlaxEngine.Vector3,FlaxEngine.ForceMode)
member.summary: Applies a force (or impulse) defined in the world space to the rigidbody at its center of mass.
member.remarks:
This will not induce any torque
ForceMode determines if the force is to be conventional or impulsive.
Each actor has an acceleration and a velocity change accumulator which are directly modified using the modes ForceMode.Acceleration and ForceMode.VelocityChange respectively. The modes ForceMode.Force and ForceMode.Impulse also modify these same accumulators and are just short hand for multiplying the vector parameter by inverse mass and then using ForceMode.Acceleration and ForceMode.VelocityChange respectively.
member.param: The force/impulse to apply defined in the world space.
The mode to use when applying the force/impulse.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.AddForceAtPosition(FlaxEngine.Vector3,FlaxEngine.Vector3,FlaxEngine.ForceMode)
member.summary: Applies a force (or impulse) defined in the world space to the rigidbody at given position in the world space.
member.remarks:
Also applies appropriate amount of torque
ForceMode determines if the force is to be conventional or impulsive.
Each actor has an acceleration and a velocity change accumulator which are directly modified using the modes ForceMode.Acceleration and ForceMode.VelocityChange respectively. The modes ForceMode.Force and ForceMode.Impulse also modify these same accumulators and are just short hand for multiplying the vector parameter by inverse mass and then using ForceMode.Acceleration and ForceMode.VelocityChange respectively.
member.param: The force/impulse to apply defined in the world space.
The position of the force/impulse in the world space.
The mode to use when applying the force/impulse.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.RigidBody.SetSolverIterationCounts(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Sets the solver iteration counts for the rigidbody.
member.remarks:
The solver iteration count determines how accurately joints and contacts are resolved. If you are having trouble with jointed bodies oscillating and behaving erratically, then setting a higher position iteration count may improve their stability.
If intersecting bodies are being depenetrated too violently, increase the number of velocity iterations. More velocity iterations will drive the relative exit velocity of the intersecting objects closer to the correct value given the restitution.
Default: 4 position iterations, 1 velocity iteration.
member.param: The minimum number of position iterations the solver should perform for this body.
The minimum number of velocity iterations the solver should perform for this body.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Collider.ComputePenetration(FlaxEngine.Collider,FlaxEngine.Collider,FlaxEngine.Vector3@,System.Single@)
member.summary: Computes minimum translational distance between two geometry objects. Translating the first collider by direction * distance will separate the colliders apart if the function returned true. Otherwise, direction and distance are not defined. The one of the colliders has to be BoxCollider, SphereCollider CapsuleCollider or a convex MeshCollider. The other one can be any type. If objects do not overlap, the function can not compute the distance and returns false.
member.param: The computed direction along which the translation required to separate the colliders apart is minimal. Valid only if function returns true.
The penetration distance along direction that is required to separate the colliders apart. Valid only if function returns true.
member.returns: True if the distance has successfully been computed, i.e. if objects do overlap, otherwise false.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ConvexMeshGenerationFlags.SkipValidation
member.summary: Disables the convex mesh validation to speed-up hull creation. Creating a convex mesh with invalid input data without prior validation may result in undefined behavior.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ConvexMeshGenerationFlags.UsePlaneShifting
member.summary:
Enables plane shifting vertex limit algorithm.
Plane shifting is an alternative algorithm for the case when the computed hull has more vertices than the specified vertex limit.
The default algorithm computes the full hull, and an OBB around the input vertices. This OBB is then sliced with the hull planes until the vertex limit is reached. The default algorithm requires the vertex limit to be set to at least 8, and typically produces results that are much better quality than are produced by plane shifting.
When plane shifting is enabled, the hull computation stops when vertex limit is reached.The hull planes are then shifted to contain all input vertices, and the new plane intersection points are then used to generate the final hull with the given vertex limit.Plane shifting may produce sharp edges to vertices very far away from the input cloud, and does not guarantee that all input vertices are inside the resulting hull. However, it can be used with a vertex limit as low as 4.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ConvexMeshGenerationFlags.UseFastInteriaComputation
member.summary: Inertia tensor computation is faster using SIMD code, but the precision is lower, which may result in incorrect inertia for very thin hulls.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ConvexMeshGenerationFlags.ShiftVertices
member.summary: Convex hull input vertices are shifted to be around origin to provide better computation stability. It is recommended to provide input vertices around the origin, otherwise use this flag to improve numerical stability.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ConvexMeshGenerationFlags.SuppressFaceRemapTable
member.summary: If checked, the face remap table is not created. This saves a significant amount of memory, but disabled ability to remap the cooked collision geometry into original mesh using raycast hit info.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ConvexMeshGenerationFlags.FastCook
member.summary: The combination of flags that improve the collision data cooking performance at the cost of quality and features. Recommend for runtime dynamic or deformable objects that need quick collision updates.

member.name: T:FlaxEngine.D6JointDriveType
member.summary: Type of drives that can be used for moving or rotating bodies attached to the joint.
member.remarks:
Each drive is an implicit force-limited damped spring: force = spring * (target position - position) + damping * (targetVelocity - velocity)
Alternatively, the spring may be configured to generate a specified acceleration instead of a force.
A linear axis is affected by drive only if the corresponding drive flag is set.There are two possible models for angular drive : swing / twist, which may be used to drive one or more angular degrees of freedom, or slerp, which may only be used to drive all three angular degrees simultaneously.

member.summary: Linear movement on the Z axis using the linear drive model.

member.summary: Rotation around the Y axis using the twist/swing angular drive model. Should not be used together with Slerp mode.

member.summary: Rotation around the Z axis using the twist/swing angular drive model. Should not be used together with Slerp mode.

member.summary: Rotation using spherical linear interpolation. Uses the SLERP angular drive mode which performs rotation by interpolating the quaternion values directly over the shortest path (applies to all three axes, which they all must be unlocked).

member.name: T:FlaxEngine.PhysicsBroadPhaseType
member.summary: Broad phase algorithm used in the simulation.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.PhysicsBroadPhaseType.SweepAndPrune
member.summary: 3-axes sweep-and-prune. Good generic choice with great performance when many objects are sleeping.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.PhysicsBroadPhaseType.MultiBoxPruning
member.summary: Alternative broad phase algorithm that does not suffer from the same performance issues as SAP when all objects are moving or when inserting large numbers of objects.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.PhysicsBroadPhaseType.AutomaticBoxPruning
member.summary: Revisited implementation of MBP, which automatically manages broad-phase regions.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.PhysicsBroadPhaseType.ParallelAutomaticBoxPruning
member.summary: Parallel implementation of ABP. It can often be the fastest (CPU) broadphase, but it can use more memory than ABP.

member.name: T:FlaxEngine.PhysicsSolverType

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.PhysicsSolverType.ProjectedGaussSeidelIterativeSolver
member.summary: The iterative sequential impulse solver.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.PhysicsSolverType.TemporalGaussSeidelSolver
member.summary: Non linear iterative solver. This kind of solver can lead to improved convergence and handle large mass ratios, long chains and jointed systems better. It is slightly more expensive than the default solver and can introduce more energy to correct joint and contact errors.

member.name: T:FlaxEngine.PhysicsCombineMode
member.summary: Enumeration that determines the way in which two material properties will be combined to yield a friction or restitution coefficient for a collision.
member.remarks: Physics doesn't have any inherent combinations because the coefficients are determined empirically on a case by case basis. However, simulating this with a pairwise lookup table is often impractical. The effective combine mode for the pair is maximum(material0.combineMode, material1.combineMode).

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.PhysicsCombineMode.Average
member.summary: Uses the average value of the touching materials: (a+b)/2.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.PhysicsCombineMode.Minimum
member.summary: Uses the smaller value of the touching materials: min(a,b)

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.PhysicsCombineMode.Multiply
member.summary: Multiplies the values of the touching materials: a*b

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.PhysicsCombineMode.Maximum
member.summary: Uses the larger value of the touching materials: max(a, b)

member.name: T:FlaxEngine.ForceMode
member.summary: Force mode type determines the exact operation that is carried out when applying the force on a rigidbody.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ForceMode.Force
member.summary: Add a continuous force to the rigidbody, using its mass. The parameter has unit of mass * distance / time^2, i.e. a force.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ForceMode.Impulse
member.summary: Add an instant force impulse to the rigidbody, using its mass. The parameter has unit of mass * distance / time.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ForceMode.VelocityChange
member.summary: Add an instant velocity change to the rigidbody, ignoring its mass. The parameter has unit of distance / time, i.e. the effect is mass independent: a velocity change.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.ForceMode.Acceleration
member.summary: Add a continuous acceleration to the rigidbody, ignoring its mass. The parameter has unit of distance / time^2, i.e. an acceleration. It gets treated just like a force except the mass is not divided out before integration.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.CollisionsHelper.RayIntersectsRay(FlaxEngine.Ray@,FlaxEngine.Ray@,FlaxEngine.Vector3@)
member.summary: Determines whether there is an intersection between a and a .
member.param: When the method completes, contains the point of intersection, or if there was no intersection.
member.remarks: This method performs a ray vs ray intersection test based on the following formula from Goldman. s = det([o_2 - o_1, d_2, d_1 x d_2]) / ||d_1 x d_2||^2 t = det([o_2 - o_1, d_1, d_1 x d_2]) / ||d_1 x d_2||^2 Where o_1 is the position of the first ray, o_2 is the position of the second ray, d_1 is the normalized direction of the first ray, d_2 is the normalized direction of the second ray, det denotes the determinant of a matrix, x denotes the cross product, [ ] denotes a matrix, and || || denotes the length or magnitude of a vector.

member.remarks: This method tests if the ray intersects either the front or back of the triangle. If the ray is parallel to the triangle's plane, no intersection is assumed to have happened. If the intersection of the ray and the triangle is behind the origin of the ray, no intersection is assumed to have happened. In both cases of assumptions, this method returns false.

member.name: T:FlaxEngine.FloatR11G11B10
member.summary: Packed vector, layout: R:11 bytes, G:11 bytes, B:10 bytes. The 3D vector is packed into 32 bits as follows: a 5-bit biased exponent and 6-bit mantissa for x component, a 5-bit biased exponent and 6-bit mantissa for y component, a 5-bit biased exponent and a 5-bit mantissa for z. The z component is stored in the most significant bits and the x component in the least significant bits. No sign bits so all partial-precision numbers are positive. (Z10Y11X11): [32] ZZZZZzzz zzzYYYYY yyyyyyXX XXXxxxxx [0]

member.summary: Performs a coordinate transformation using the given .
member.param: When the method completes, contains the transformed coordinates.
member.remarks: A coordinate transform performs the transformation with the assumption that the w component is one. The four dimensional vector obtained from the transformation operation has each component in the vector divided by the w component. This forces the w component to be one and therefore makes the vector homogeneous. The homogeneous vector is often preferred when working with coordinates as the w component can safely be ignored.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Vector2.TransformNormal(FlaxEngine.Vector2@,FlaxEngine.Matrix@,FlaxEngine.Vector2@)
member.summary: Performs a normal transformation using the given .
member.param: When the method completes, contains the transformed normal.
member.remarks: A normal transform performs the transformation with the assumption that the w component is zero. This causes the fourth row and fourth column of the matrix to be unused. The end result is a vector that is not translated, but all other transformation properties apply. This is often preferred for normal vectors as normals purely represent direction rather than location because normal vectors should not be translated.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Vector3.TransformCoordinate(FlaxEngine.Vector3@,FlaxEngine.Matrix@,FlaxEngine.Vector3@)
member.summary: Performs a coordinate transformation using the given .
member.param: When the method completes, contains the transformed coordinates.
member.remarks: A coordinate transform performs the transformation with the assumption that the w component is one. The four dimensional vector obtained from the transformation operation has each component in the vector divided by the w component. This forces the w component to be one and therefore makes the vector homogeneous. The homogeneous vector is often preferred when working with coordinates as the w component can safely be ignored.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Vector3.TransformNormal(FlaxEngine.Vector3@,FlaxEngine.Matrix@,FlaxEngine.Vector3@)
member.summary: Performs a normal transformation using the given .
member.param: When the method completes, contains the transformed normal.
member.remarks: A normal transform performs the transformation with the assumption that the w component is zero. This causes the fourth row and fourth column of the matrix to be unused. The end result is a vector that is not translated, but all other transformation properties apply. This is often preferred for normal vectors as normals purely represent direction rather than location because normal vectors should not be translated.

member.summary: Asserts that the values are approximately equal. An absolute error check is used for approximate equality check (|a-b| < tolerance). Default tolerance is 0.00001f. Note: Every time you call the method with tolerance specified, a new instance of Assertions.Comparers.FloatComparer is created. For performance reasons you might want to instance your own comparer and pass it to the AreEqual method. If the tolerance is not specifies, a default comparer is used and the issue does not occur.

member.summary: Loads the data from the mesh.
member.param: The source mesh object to access.

If set to true the data will be downloaded from the GPU, otherwise it can be loaded from the drive (source asset file) or from memory (if cached). Downloading mesh from GPU requires this call to be made from the other thread than main thread. Virtual assets are always downloaded from GPU memory due to lack of dedicated storage container for the asset data.

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Object.Destroy(FlaxEngine.Object,System.Single)
member.summary: Destroys the specified object and clears the reference variable. The object obj will be destroyed now or after the time specified in seconds from now. If obj is a Script it will be removed from the Actor and deleted. If obj is an Actor it will be removed from the Scene and deleted as well as all its Scripts and all children of the Actor. Actual object destruction is always delayed until after the current Update loop, but will always be done before rendering.
member.param: The time left to destroy object (in seconds).

member.name: M:FlaxEngine.Object.DestroyNow(FlaxEngine.Object)
member.summary: Destroys the specified object and clears the reference variable. The object obj will be destroyed immediately. If obj is a Script it will be removed from the Actor and deleted. If obj is an Actor it will be removed from the Scene and deleted as well as all its Scripts and all children of the Actor.

member.name: T:FlaxEngine.CanvasRenderMode
member.summary: The canvas rendering modes.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.CanvasRenderMode.ScreenSpace
member.summary: The screen space rendering mode that places UI elements on the screen rendered on top of the scene. If the screen is resized or changes resolution, the Canvas will automatically change size to match this.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.CanvasRenderMode.CameraSpace
member.summary: The camera space rendering mode that places Canvas in a given distance in front of a specified Camera. The UI elements are rendered by this camera, which means that the Camera settings affect the appearance of the UI. If the Camera is set to Perspective, the UI elements will be rendered with perspective, and the amount of perspective distortion can be controlled by the Camera Field of View. If the screen is resized, changes resolution, or the camera frustum changes, the Canvas will automatically change size to match as well.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.CanvasRenderMode.WorldSpace
member.summary: The world space rendering mode that places Canvas as any other object in the scene. The size of the Canvas can be set manually using its Transform, and UI elements will render in front of or behind other objects in the scene based on 3D placement. This is useful for UIs that are meant to be a part of the world. This is also known as a 'diegetic interface'.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.CanvasRenderMode.WorldSpaceFaceCamera
member.summary: The world space rendering mode that places Canvas as any other object in the scene and orients it to face the camera. The size of the Canvas can be set manually using its Transform, and UI elements will render in front of or behind other objects in the scene based on 3D placement. This is useful for UIs that are meant to be a part of the world. This is also known as a 'diegetic interface'.

member.name: F:FlaxEngine.CanvasRenderMode.GPUTexture
member.summary: The off-screen rendering mode that draws the contents of the canvas into a GPU texture that can be used in the scene or by other systems. The size of the canvas is automatically set to the size of the texture.

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.OutputName
member.summary: Name of the output app created by the build system. Used to rename main executable (eg. MyGame.exe) or final package name (eg. MyGame.apk). Custom tokens: ${PROJECT_NAME}, ${COMPANY_NAME}.

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.MaxAssetsPerPackage
member.summary: The maximum amount of assets to include into a single assets package. Asset packages will split into several packages if need to.

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.MaxPackageSizeMB
member.summary: The maximum size of the single assets package (in megabytes). Asset packages will split into several packages if need to.

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.ContentKey
member.summary: The game content cooking keycode. Use the same value for a game and DLC packages to support loading them by the build game. Use 0 to randomize it during building.

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.ForDistribution
member.summary: If checked, the builds produced by the Game Cooker will be treated as for final game distribution (eg. for game store upload). Builds done this way cannot be tested on console devkits (eg. Xbox One, Xbox Scarlett). Enabled by default for `Release` builds.

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.SkipPackaging
member.summary: If checked, the output build files won't be packaged for the destination platform. Useful when debugging build from local PC.

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.AdditionalAssets
member.summary: The list of additional assets to include into build (into root assets set).

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.AdditionalScenes
member.summary: The list of additional scenes to include into build (into root assets set).

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.AdditionalAssetFolders
member.summary: The list of additional folders with assets to include into build (into root assets set). Paths relative to the project directory (or absolute).

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.ShadersNoOptimize
member.summary: Disables shaders compiler optimizations in cooked game. Can be used to debug shaders on a target platform or to speed up the shaders compilation time.

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.ShadersGenerateDebugData
member.summary: Enables shader debug data generation for shaders in cooked game (depends on the target platform rendering backend).

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.SkipDefaultFonts
member.summary: If checked, skips bundling default engine fonts for UI. Use if to reduce build size if you don't use default engine fonts but custom ones only.

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.MaxMeshPositionError
member.summary: The maximum acceptable mesh vertex position error (in world units) for data quantization. Use 0 to disable this feature. Affects meshes during import (or reimpport).

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.SkipDotnetPackaging
member.summary: If checked, .NET Runtime won't be packaged with a game and will be required by user to be installed on system upon running game build. Available only on supported platforms such as Windows, Linux and macOS.

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Content.Settings.BuildSettings.SkipUnusedDotnetLibsPackaging
member.summary: If checked, .NET Runtime packaging will skip unused libraries from packaging resulting in smaller game builds.

member.name: F:FlaxEditor.Tools.Terrain.Brushes.CircleBrush.Falloff
member.summary: The brush falloff that defines the percentage from the brush's extents where the falloff should begin. Essentially, this describes how hard the brush's edges are. A falloff of 0 means the brush will have full effect throughout with hard edges. A falloff of 1 means the brush will only have full effect at its center, and the effect will be reduced throughout its entire area to the edge.
